title: Team Lead
description:
A LITTLE BIT ABOUT Boldr

•
Boldr is the first global B-Corp dedicated to delivering world-class Client experiences while creating access to dignified, meaningful work in communities around the world.

• We are a global team, united by our desire to connect diverse people with common values for Boldr impact.

LET’S START WITH OUR VALUES

• Meaningful connections start with AUTHENTICITY

● We do our best work by being CURIOUS
● We grow by remaining DYNAMIC

• Our success combines AMBITIOUS VISION with OPERATIONAL EXCELLENCE

• At the heart of great partnerships, we’ll always find EMPATHY

WHAT IS YOUR ROLE
As a Team Lead , you are responsible for executing processes defined by the client or management. You will need to efficiently manage a large amount of often sensitive or confidential information. The role will require keen attention to detail while maintaining productivity at defined proficiency levels.
WHY DO WE WANT YOU
We are currently looking for impact-driven individuals who are passionate in helping Boldr grow and achieve our Purpose. We expect our Team to become our ultimate partners to success by always giving their 110% in everything, sharing their talents and quirks, and championing our core values: Curious, Dynamic, and Authentic.
WHAT WILL YOU DO

• Team Leadership: Supervise and lead a team of team members during the assigned shift. Provide guidance, coaching, and support to ensure team members meet their goals and objectives.

• Quality Assurance: Ensure support and acknowledgment of quality standards aligned with our client and customer experience. Implement quality control procedures and address any quality issues promptly.

• Performance Metrics: Monitor and track key performance metrics, such as agent tasks and responsibilities. Take corrective actions as needed to meet or exceed performance targets.

• Training and Development: Train new associates and provide ongoing training to existing team members to enhance their skills and knowledge. Foster a culture of continuous improvements through weekly 1:1s and impromptu coaching sessions.

• Communication: Maintain open and effective communication channels with team members, other shift leads, and management. Report any issues, escalations, or opportunities for improvement.

• Problem Solving: Address operational challenges and resolve issues that may arise during the shift. Collaborate with other departments to find solutions to complex problems.

• Helpdesk Management: Ensure the helpdesk is managed by checking agent availability and SLA tickets.

• Ensuring you are available as the POC in the management queue to do escalations.

Requirements
WHAT WE’LL LIKE ABOUT YOU
YOU ARE…

• Curious and authentic, just like us! #beboldr

• An analytical and critical thinker, with an eye for even the most minute of details

● Passionate about client satisfaction
YOU HAVE…

• Bachelor's/College Degree in any field you’re passionate about!

● 1 year of leadership experience.

• 2+ years of Customer Support experience

• Basic knowledge of cloud-based applications such as Google Drive, Google Sheets, Google Docs, and MS Office applications.

• Familiarity with help desk or ticketing systems (Intercom experience a plus).

• Familiarity with website-building tools, content management systems, or presentation software

• Strong technical aptitude for troubleshooting digital platforms and web-based apps.

• Excellent verbal and written communication skills.

• An ability to understand and communicate complex ideas to clients.

• Ability to accept feedback gracefully and with an open mind.

• Customer orientation and ability to adapt/respond to customers with diverse backgrounds.

NICE TO HAVE...

• Knowledge of presentation software (Gamma, PowerPoint, Google Slides, Canva).

• Familiarity with AI-powered tools or generative platforms.

title: Member Implementation Advisor
description:
About Better Impact
At Better Impact , we believe technology should make it easier for organizations to do meaningful work. Our software helps nonprofits, hospitals, government agencies, and other organizations manage their volunteer programs, streamline operations, and strengthen community engagement.
Backed by The Brydon Group, Better Impact is growing, and we're looking for thoughtful, collaborative people who are excited to help our members get the most out of the technology they use every day.
About the Role
We're looking for a Member Implementation Advisor to help new members successfully launch and adopt Better Impact software.
In this role, you'll be part trainer, part problem-solver, and part trusted guide. You'll work directly with new members to understand their goals, navigate implementation, and build the skills and confidence they need to use our software effectively.
Successful implementation isn't just about getting software up and running. It's about helping people understand how technology can support their work, identifying practical solutions to their challenges, and creating a positive experience from the very beginning.
You'll receive training on our software, implementation processes, and member experience standards, gradually taking on greater responsibility as you become familiar with our products and approach.
If you enjoy teaching others, solving problems, building relationships, and helping organizations succeed, this could be a great fit.
Location & Working Hours
This is a fully remote position open to candidates located in the United States or Canada.
Candidates must be available to work Pacific or Mountain Time Zone business hours, regardless of their physical location, to support our members effectively.
What You'll Do
Guide Members Through Implementation

• Work directly with new members to understand their goals, existing processes, and operational needs.

• Help members develop practical implementation strategies that align with their organization's priorities.

• Guide members through the implementation process, from initial onboarding through successful software adoption.

• Identify challenges, recommend solutions, and help members make informed decisions about how to configure and use the software.
Deliver Training and Build Confidence

• Lead engaging, accessible software training sessions for individuals and groups.

• Adapt your communication and teaching approach to different audiences, experience levels, and learning styles.

• Explain software features and workflows in ways that are clear, approachable, and relevant to each member's needs.

• Help members develop the knowledge and confidence to manage their software independently.
Create a Great Member Experience

• Build positive, professional relationships with members throughout their implementation journey.

• Maintain clear communication, manage expectations, and ensure members understand next steps.

• Introduce members to additional tools, resources, and services that may support their goals.

• Collaborate with colleagues across teams to resolve challenges and ensure a smooth member experience.
Contribute to Continuous Improvement

• Maintain accurate records of implementation activities, member progress, and follow-up needs.

• Identify opportunities to improve implementation processes, training materials, and the overall member experience.

• Share member feedback and insights with internal teams to support ongoing improvements.
Requirements
We're interested in candidates who bring a combination of technical aptitude, strong communication skills, and a genuine interest in helping others succeed.
Qualifications

• Experience in a client-facing role, ideally within a SaaS or technology environment, such as implementation, customer success, onboarding, training, or operations.

• Strong communication and presentation skills, with the ability to explain technical concepts clearly to audiences with varying levels of experience.

title: PIP Claims Handler
description:
This is a remote position.
Position Summary:
We are seeking an experienced PIP Claims Handler to manage and investigate Personal Injury Protection (PIP) claims related to automotive accidents. This role is heavily focused on reviewing claims for accuracy, identifying inconsistencies, mitigating fraud exposure, and controlling claim costs while ensuring compliance with state regulations and policy requirements.
The ideal candidate has extensive experience handling PIP claims within the auto insurance, legal, healthcare billing, or claims administration space and is highly skilled at scrutinizing medical documentation, billing practices, and treatment timelines.
This position requires strong analytical ability, attention to detail, and confidence in challenging questionable claims, excessive billing, or unsupported treatment.
Essential Duties and Responsibilities (include, but are not limited to the following):
Key Responsibilities

• This role primarily handles PIP claims arising in Maryland, with regular exposure to Pennsylvania, Florida, Georgia, Illinois, Virginia, and the District of Columbia. Familiarity with the regulatory frameworks in any of these states is strongly preferred; mastery of Maryland PIP is required

• Review, investigate, and manage PIP claims from initial notice through resolution

• Analyze medical records, treatment plans, billing submissions, police reports, and supporting documentation

• Identify billing irregularities, excessive treatment patterns, duplicate charges, inflated claims, or potential fraud indicators

• Evaluate claim validity and determine exposure based on applicable state PIP regulations and policy guidelines

• Defend against inaccurate, unsupported, or excessive claims through detailed file review and documentation

• Coordinate with attorneys, medical providers, adjusters, third-party administrators, and internal stakeholders

• Negotiate settlements and reductions with providers, attorneys, and claimants when appropriate

• Monitor claim timelines and ensure all statutory deadlines and compliance requirements are met

• Prepare detailed claim notes, summaries, and recommendations for leadership or legal review

• Assist with litigation support and respond to disputes, arbitrations, or audits related to PIP claims

• Identify trends and recommend process improvements to reduce claim leakage and financial exposure

• Maintain accurate claim files and documentation within internal systems

Qualifications Required:

• 3+ years of direct experience handling automotive PIP claims

• Strong knowledge of PIP regulations, medical billing review, and claims investigation practices

• Experience defending against questionable or inflated PIP claims

• Ability to interpret medical records, treatment documentation, and billing codes

• Experience in identifying fraud indicators, provider abuse, or claim inconsistencies

• Strong negotiation and conflict-resolution skills

• Excellent organizational skills and attention to detail

• Ability to manage a high-volume caseload while maintaining accuracy

• Proficient in claims management systems and Microsoft Office / Google Workspace

Preferred Qualifications:

• Experience in rideshare, fleet, rental, or commercial auto claims environments

• Prior experience working with SIU (Special Investigations Unit) teams

• Familiarity with state-specific PIP regulations, especially high-volume PIP states

• Experience working with attorneys and litigation management

• Insurance adjuster license(s) where applicable

Salary: $65,000 - $70,000 per year; depending on experience
Ideal Candidate Profile
The ideal candidate is highly detail-oriented, skeptical in the right ways, and comfortable challenging unsupported claims or questionable documentation. They should be able to balance thorough investigation with efficient claim handling and understand how to reduce unnecessary claim spend without compromising compliance or professionalism.

title: Head of Pricing & Monetization (m/f/d)
description:
About Babbel Labs

Babbel Labs is building the future of language learning. We're an AI-first, independent company within the Babbel group, based in Berlin. Our teams bring AI, R&D and product together to ship experiences that set a new standard for how people learn.

Your Learning Journey in This Role

We are looking for a Head of Pricing & Monetization to define and evolve Babbel’s pricing, packaging and monetization strategy. You will lead pricing decisions across existing and new products, including subscription plans, family plans, add-ons, trials and offers.

This is a hands-on individual-contributor role, with the opportunity to build a pricing function over time. You will work across Product, Growth, Marketing, Finance, Data and Engineering to turn customer insight and commercial analysis into pricing decisions that improve sustainable growth.

How You’ll Make an Impact

- Own Babbel’s pricing and monetization strategy across products, markets and customer segments, and develop the frameworks and processes behind it.

- Design pricing and packaging for new products and models, including subscription options, family plans and add-ons.

- Lead pricing decisions for existing plans, free trials, offers and customer segments, from analysis and modelling through to cross-functional alignment and launch.

- Establish clear principles for discounts, promotions and offers across Marketing and CRM, and improve pricing pages, checkout and subscription flows.

- Measure the impact of pricing decisions on revenue, conversion, retention and acquisition costs, using experimentation and analysis to continuously improve performance.

 

Your Skills and Qualifications

We think you’ll need the following experience to succeed in the role:

- Senior-level experience owning pricing or monetization in a fast-growing technology, subscription, digital product or consumer business.

- A proven track record of leading significant pricing or packaging changes end to end, from customer and market insight through to modelling, stakeholder alignment, launch and post-launch measurement.

- Experience building or scaling pricing capabilities, frameworks or ways of working, and partnering with Product, Engineering, Growth, Marketing, Finance and Data teams.

In addition, here are the skills and capabilities we’re looking for:

- Commercial and strategic judgement: Understands how pricing and packaging affect revenue, conversion, retention, customer acquisition and long-term customer value, and can make sound trade-offs.

- Quantitative and technical fluency: Comfortable with pricing methods such as elasticity analysis, willingness-to-pay research, segmentation, forecasting and experiment analysis. Able to build models, work with data and use code where appropriate.

- Product execution and experimentation: Translates pricing strategy into clear product requirements, experiments and launches. Uses AI tools and coding agents to prototype, test and iterate efficiently.

- Communication, influence and ownership: Explains complex analysis clearly to both technical and executive audiences, persuades senior stakeholders, creates clarity in ambiguous situations and drives decisions through to completion.

WAYS OF WORKING

You will work across Product, Growth, Marketing, Finance, Data and Engineering, building alignment around pricing decisions and helping teams move from analysis to action.

The role requires strong analytical depth, commercial judgement and hands-on execution. You should be comfortable working independently, challenging assumptions constructively and taking ownership without a large team around you.

Babbel’s operating language is English, so professional fluency in written and spoken English is required.

Please note that our company’s operating language is English, so you will need to be able to work in English.

Why Join Babbel Labs

- Work on a mission-driven product with global impact.

- Shape how AI is used responsibly in education.

title: Cruise Sales Advisor - US

Since launching in early 2025 it has become the digital home for 145,000+ cruisers, co-founded with Emma Cruises, one of the world's most influential cruise content creators, and her audience of over half a million people across YouTube and social.
The Cruise Globe Agency is the booking arm of that ecosystem. We intend for The Cruise Globe to become the world's leading cruise agency within a decade. We believe we have the data, the audience, the network and the team to do it - and this role is part of building that.
This is a content and data led agency, where real, trusted, expert human advisors convert genuine, high-intent demand from our community.

In the press: Travel Weekly - “ The Cruise Globe hopes new agency will be world leader within a decade”
About the Role
This is an in-country, customer-facing Cruise Advisor role. You will handle high-intent enquiries from the Globe platform and Emma Cruises' audience, end to end - from first conversation through to a confirmed, well-serviced booking.
Customers will come back to you, refer their friends to you, and ask for you by name. That is the point of the role: we are building a team of named, visible, expert advisors for our community, not an anonymous call centre.
You will report to the Head of US Agency, and you will also be supported by a sales support team who filter enquiries and handle pre-cruise admin, so your time goes where it matters - advising and closing.
The agency is growing rapidly and there is a genuine path to progress to Senior Cruise Advisor and, in time, Sales Manager.
What You Will Do
1. Advise and close, end to end

• Take high-intent inbound enquiries by phone and email from the Globe platform and Emma Cruises' audience.

• Build genuine rapport quickly - we want you to build long-standing relationships with your customers.

• Design itineraries and quotes, and close cruise bookings across mainstream, premium and select luxury lines.

• Book the whole trip where it adds value - air, hotels, transfers, insurance and extras - not just the cruise.

• Handle group bookings (milestone birthdays, anniversaries, reunions) confidently and accurately.

2. Be the guest’s trusted point of contact

• Be the primary point of contact for your guests throughout the journey - the person they come back to, refer their friends to, and ask for by name.

• Keep the CRM accurate and up to date - clean records, logged conversations and preferences are how guests are looked after properly and handed between advisors without anything being dropped.

• Run a proactive post-booking service - pre-cruise touchpoints, price monitoring, and being genuinely useful before, during and after the trip.

• Drive repeat bookings and referrals; treat the lifetime of the guest relationship, not the single transaction, as the goal.

3. Protect the brand

• Give honest, unbiased advice. Our credibility is built on Emma's content and a community of over half a million cruisers - we never put commission ahead of the right recommendation.

• Handle problems and crisis situations calmly, with the customer's interest first

• Operate to a high standard of accuracy on fares, cabins, payment schedules and documentation.

4. Work as part of a remote team

• Excel in a fully remote, fast-paced environment - you should be self-directed, disciplined, and reliable without anyone looking over your shoulder.

• Follow the agency's processes and QA standards - and feed back honestly when something can be done better.

• Use the Globe platform's data on each customer (their wishlists, viewed itineraries and history) to know them before the first call.

title: Senior Customer Support Service Delivery Program Manager
locationText: San Francisco, CA, New York, NY, Portland, OR, or Remote within Canada or United States
description:
In 1931, electrical draftsman Harry Beck looked at London’s Underground map and saw a system that had become too complicated to understand.

The maps at the time tried to represent the city geographically. Beck realized that wasn’t what riders actually needed. What mattered was how the system connected: which lines went where, where you could transfer, and the simplest way to get from one place to another. So he redrew the network around those relationships instead. His design became the foundation for the modern Tube map and changed how people navigated London.

Mercury’s Customer Experience organization has its own increasingly complex network.

As Mercury grows, the right place for support work will keep changing. Some new or complex work may benefit from starting in an incubation team before we know how it should scale. From there, it might move into Core Support, remain specialized, transition to an outsourced partner, or become increasingly supported by AI-powered tooling. The challenge is knowing where work belongs at each stage of its lifecycle, when it’s ready to move, and how to make those transitions without compromising the customer experience.

For the first 9-12 months, a significant majority of your work will focus on our growing BPO partnership. You’ll identify opportunities to expand the work we deliver through that partnership, build the operational and financial case for doing so, align CX leadership around those recommendations, and lead approved transitions from initial scoping through stabilization.

Over time, the scope will broaden. You’ll apply the same thinking across our wider service delivery ecosystem, helping us evaluate when work should enter an incubation model, when it is ready to graduate, and whether its next home should be Core Support, a specialized team, an outsourced partner, AI-powered tooling, or another model as our capabilities evolve.

You won’t be the sole decision-maker on where work lives. Your role is to develop the recommendation: bring together the data, customer impact, operational realities, and tradeoffs; build a compelling case; and help CX leadership reach a well-informed decision. Once a direction is approved, you’ll own the program that turns it into reality.

This is a role for someone who can move fluidly between strategy and execution. You should be equally energized by building a strong argument for how our service delivery model should evolve and by working through the operational details required to make that change succeed.

In this role, you will:

• Lead high-impact programs that evolve how CX delivers support, with the first 9-12 months heavily focused on expanding and optimizing our BPO partnership.

• Identify opportunities to move work to a different service delivery model and build the case for change using customer, operational, and financial data. This could include recommending that emerging or complex work move into incubation, as well as determining when incubated work is mature enough to transition into Core Support, a specialized team, or our BPO partnership.

• Help define what makes work ready to move. Develop clear criteria for when a workflow needs incubation, when it has reached sufficient maturity and stability to graduate, and which delivery model is best positioned to own it next.

• Evaluate where AI-powered tooling could take on, augment, or reshape support work, and partner with the right teams to build a clear case for when automation creates a better customer and business outcome.

• Lead approved service delivery transitions end to end, whether work is moving into incubation, graduating from incubation, transitioning between internal teams, or moving to an outsourced partner. Own the program from initial scoping and business case through readiness, migration, ramp, stabilization, and handoff into long-term operations.

• Partner across Workforce Management, Enablement, QA, Support, and other teams to build transition plans that account

title: BSA/AML Officer - US
description:
ABOUT ARQ

ARQ is one of the fastest-growing fintechs in the world. Our mission is to redefine how people interact with money across borders, building the backbone to move value seamlessly. We’re still early in our journey, which means every person who joins shapes the future of our product, culture, and growth. If you’re excited by big challenges, global impact, and the chance to grow fast with a world-class team, ARQ is the place to do it.

THE JOB

You find risk, measure it and call it. You do not fix it.

Every finding you write answers three things: what is broken, how bad it is, and what evidence proves it. You don't soften the rating and you don't propose the remedy. The business owns the fix. You own the truth about the risk.

WHAT YOU WILL DO

- Test our BSA/AML, KYC, OFAC and transaction monitoring controls end to end, independently of the teams that run them

- Rate every finding (high / medium / low) with evidence that holds up in front of a regulator

- Pull and analyze data yourself; you don't wait for someone to send you a report

- Challenge thresholds, alert logic and sampling assumptions with numbers, not opinions

- Track open issues until owners close them, and escalate when they don't

- Prepare us for regulator exams and audits, and be the person in the room who already knows the weak spots

WHAT YOU NEED (NON-NEGOTIABLE)

- 4+ years in BSA/AML, FinCrime, internal audit or regulatory compliance

- Experience at a top-tier audit/advisory firm, in-house compliance, or both. Both is ideal.

- You have written findings that a regulator, auditor or board actually read

- You can say "this is high risk" to a senior leader and point to the regulation which proves it.

- Deep working knowledge of the BSA, USA PATRIOT Act, OFAC and FinCEN expectations

NICE TO HAVE

- Law degree (JD) or bar admission

- Degree in engineering, mathematics, statistics or another STEM field

- SQL: you can query transaction data yourself

- Python or R for analysis, sampling or testing alert logic

- Statistics: sampling design, hypothesis testing, threshold and model validation

- CAMS, CRCM, CIA, CISA, CPA or CFE

- Exposure to AI or model risk (SR 11-7, NIST AI RMF)

YOU WILL NOT ENJOY THIS ROLE IF

- You need someone else to pull the data for you

- You round risk ratings down to keep people comfortable

- You are uncomfortable being the person no one wants in the meeting

- You uniform to the norm.

title: Staff Machine Learning Engineer, Data Curation & Dataset Strategy
description:
Before the detail, here's the challenge you'd help us solve.

We build the embodied intelligence that moves real vehicles safely, and the ecosystem a billion machines will run on in the future. Very few people in AI can say this. Every role here, whatever the team, plugs into that.

Here’s what this particular role covers.

🛠️ About our datasets Team

Wayve's datasets team own the driving data that our AI Driver learns from, covering ingestion, annotation, retrieval and data quality. As our data grows from hundreds of petabytes towards exabyte scale, deciding what we keep, and where, is one of the biggest levers on both model quality and cost. This role sits at the centre of that challenge, shaping the data that model engineers train on across the company.

 

🧠 Your day-to-day

- Build and own the ingestion-time model that scores incoming driving data and routes it to hot, cold, archive or delete

- Work with training teams to define the right data distributions for every model we're building

- Deliver early storage-cost savings through practical heuristics, then develop ML-driven filtering

- Partner with ingestion, annotation, retrieval, data quality, model training, AV/robotics, evaluation and storage teams to set company-wide data policy

- Lead and work hands-on with a small group of software and ML engineers to build data provisioning and data provenance features into Corpus

 

🧩 What you’ll be working on

- Defining our dataset content strategy: which data and metadata we need, and why, so training teams can select the most valuable data as smoothly as possible

- Steering data selection by what our model engineers need right now. For example, if we're weak at unprotected right turns at traffic lights, those scenarios go straight to hot storage

- Delivering large, measurable storage-cost savings as ingestion scales across our internal fleet and partner and OEM data

- Evolving from practical heuristics to ML-driven filtering, and influencing what gets filtered at the vehicle and edge

- Working as a pair with our Corpus Implementation Engineer to turn strategy into production systems

 

🙌 You should apply if

- You have strong autonomous-vehicle or robotics experience, working with large-scale driving, sensor or comparable data

- You're a principal, hands-on ML engineer who has built models that score, select or filter data

- You've operated at petabyte scale and are comfortable with the engineering that comes with it

- You're strong in Python and Spark, with large-scale cloud data experience

- You have strong quantitative intuition and use it to make practical, measurable decisions

- You're pragmatic and high-ownership, and can set direction across several teams without direct authority

- You bring experience in data selection, retention or filtering for model training, edge or vehicle-side filtering, computer vision or high-volume IoT data, or leading small cross-functional groups (any of these is a bonus)

 

🌱 Not ticking every box? That’s totally okay! If you’re passionate about autonomy and keen to learn, we encourage you to apply even if you don’t meet every requirement.

 

More about Wayve:

🚀 Wayve is building the leading AI platform for autonomous driving. We are pioneering an end to end AI approach that enables vehicles to learn directly from real world experience, developing the ability to adapt, generalise and improve at scale. Instead of relying on hand coded rules or pre mapped environments, our AI Driver learns to drive by understanding the world around it. The result is technology that navigates complex urban environments with intelligence, precision and natural flow, unlocking meaningful advances in both safety and efficiency. We believe autonomy represents a once in a generation transformation in how people and goods move, comparable to the shift from horses to cars, and from human driven vehicles to intelligent machines.

title: Field Service Engineer
description:
About the Team

OpenAI's infrastructure teams design, build, activate, and operate the critical systems that support large-scale AI compute. Field Service Engineering partners across design, construction, commissioning, site operations, hardware operations, and equipment providers to turn complex infrastructure into safe, reliable, and serviceable systems.

About the Role

We are seeking a senior, field service engineer to build the technical operating model responsible for critical electrical and mechanical infrastructure across our data center portfolio. This is a field-oriented electrical & mechanical engineering role, not a traditional facilities operations position. You will combine deep systems understanding in data center power and cooling systems to aid in SOO, design, maintenance & operability, troubleshooting and other engineering related responsibility around key equipment. The role will include leveraging training and experience to establish standards, develop people, coordinate vendors, and drive issues from design, first principles, first signals through verified resolution. The strongest candidates will have deep expertise in either electrical and mechanical systems and strong working fluency across the other discipline (e.g. controls, business acumen).

Remote - travel 50%

In this role, you will:

- Lead field support for startup, commissioning, troubleshooting, repair, and reliability improvement across critical data center infrastructure.

- Serve as the senior technical owner for transformers, switchgear, UPS systems, generators, PDUs, protection and controls, chillers, cooling towers, pumps, CDUs, CRAH units, and associated control systems.

- Diagnose complex failures across power, cooling, controls, and hardware interfaces; distinguish symptoms from root causes and drive corrective actions through validation.

- Build the field service operating model, including staffing recommendations, coverage, escalation paths, response expectations, spare-parts strategy, documentation, and performance metrics.

- Aid in hiring, development, and coaching other field service engineers and technicians while creating a culture of safety, technical rigor, accountability, and continuous learning.

- Partner with design, construction, commissioning, site operations, and hardware teams to improve maintainability, readiness, and lifecycle reliability.

- Manage OEM and service-provider relationships, technical escalations, repair plans, warranties, and sustained corrective action.

- Establish and improve safe work practices, including lockout/tagout, switching and maintenance procedures, MOPs, SOPs, EOPs, and incident response.

- Translate field learning into design feedback, preventive maintenance improvements, training, and reusable standards.

You might thrive in this role if you have:

- 8+ years of hands-on experience supporting critical electrical, mechanical, or electromechanical infrastructure in data centers, industrial facilities, utilities, manufacturing, or similarly complex environments.

- Deep technical expertise in at least one discipline, electrical or mechanical, with demonstrated ability to troubleshoot across electromechanical and controls boundaries.

- Experience building, leading, or materially developing a field engineering, service, maintenance, or technician team.

- Demonstrated success leading high-severity troubleshooting, root-cause analysis, corrective action, and reliability improvement.

- Ability to read and use one-line diagrams, schematics, P&IDs, sequence-of-operations documents, control diagrams, equipment manuals, and commissioning records.

- Strong safety judgment and experience working under formal energization, isolation, maintenance, and change-control procedures.

- Clear written and verbal communication with engineers, technicians, vendors, construction teams, and senior stakeholders.

- Ability to travel up to 50% and support planned or urgent field activity when required.

title: Senior Incident Responder
description:

We defend our clients’ digital lives from hackers, privacy leaks, and identity theft. If you are passionate about helping to protect others, then keep reading - this may be your next great opportunity.

BlackCloak is seeking a seasoned and highly skilled Senior Incident Responder to join our Technical Success Team. This is a senior, client-facing individual contributor role for someone who has spent years on both sides of the problem: the technical compromise of computers, phones, and online accounts, and the financial fraud that so often follows it. In this critical role, you will serve as the primary escalation point and lead investigator for complex security events; taking ownership of the full incident response lifecycle, from initial triage and containment through eradication, recovery, and post-incident reporting.

Our clients are executives, board members, and high-profile individuals whose personal accounts and devices are targeted precisely because their corporate ones are hard to breach. When something goes wrong in a client's personal digital life, you are the person who takes the call, works the incident end to end, and stays with them until it is resolved. You will also help us get better at preventing the next one: mapping how each incident unfolded against both the cyber attack kill chain and the personal attack kill chain, closing the gaps that made it possible, and mentoring the responders behind you.

If you excel at guiding clients through high-stress situations, possess deep technical expertise in digital forensics, and have a proven track record of handling sophisticated threats targeting high-profile individuals, this is an opportunity to elevate your career and make a tangible impact.

What You Will Do

• Execute End-to-End Incident Response: Lead comprehensive incident handling consistent with core IR principles (NIST/SANS) from the initial client request and triage through containment, recovery, and post-incident lessons learned.

• Investigate Complex Compromises & Targeted Attacks: Manage and remediate severe client security incidents, including but not limited to, compromised email ecosystems, SIM swap attacks, financial account takeovers, and targeted credential harvesting.

• Device Analysis: Conduct analysis on client computers and mobile devices to assess the scope of compromise and implement effective remediation strategies.

• Remediate Fraud & Identity Theft: Analyze and assess account activity and transaction records available to the client on their email, banking, retail, and social platforms to help establish what occurred, and support clients in their conversations with the platforms on fraud investigations, disputes, account freezes, etc.. Guide identity theft victims through the remediation process - credit bureau freezes and fraud alerts, IdentityTheft.gov and law enforcement reporting - and advise clients on the activity they should watch for and report back to the team.

• Map the Attack Chain: Map observed activity against the personal attack kill chain - from data-broker reconnaissance and social engineering of the client's inner circle through device compromise, account takeover, and financial monetization - to identify the likely stage of an attack and the actions that break the chain, focusing on technique and exposure rather than actor attribution.

• Provide White-Glove Client Support: Interface directly with clients and, where authorized, their families and support staff - assistants, family office, corporate security - during high-stakes emergency onboardings and active incidents, providing calm, clear, and authoritative guidance while communicating complex threat assessments.

About Feanix Bio

Feanix is rebuilding animal breeding from the genome up.

We’re a YC-backed startup using whole-genome sequencing and custom ML models to help dairy farmers make better breeding and herd management decisions. Our technology is genuinely novel: we can sequence a full genome from a single hair at a fraction of traditional industry costs, our models achieve ~90% prediction accuracy on traits where existing approaches sit closer to ~30%, and we’re pioneering farm-specific genomic predictions that turn genetics into practical, actionable decisions.

That technology is translating into real adoption. In a short time, we’ve grown to serve roughly 1% of the U.S. dairy industry, with many customers in the pipeline. We started with dairy because our founders grew up on dairy farms and understand firsthand the problems we’re solving. But genetics is foundational to every agricultural industry, and dairy is only the beginning.

We’re building Feanix with a small, high-caliber team where people have meaningful ownership and work end to end. There are no unnecessary layers and very little room for busywork - just difficult problems at the intersection of biology, data, and software that haven’t been solved before.

If you’re exceptional at what you do and want your work to have a measurable impact on an entire industry, we’d love to build it with you.

About The Role
Feanix is expanding its product offerings based on our farmers' needs and moving into other species, and engineering has to scale with these business goals. Today we're a small, tight engineering team behind one core product: Autopilot and sire mating, the decision engine farmers act on every day. We're shifting from individuals carrying whole systems to teams that share them, and we're growing in close partnership with our product organization. Over the next 12-18 months we plan to grow engineering to around 30 people. The technology organization includes software, hardware, and product, and this role leads software development.
You'll be our first Director of Engineering, reporting to the CTO. You'll lead a team of engineering managers: two have already joined, and you'll hire more to support the organization's growth. Our staff and principal engineers, who lead architecture, also report directly to you rather than to the EMs. You run the engineering org and its delivery, and you set technical direction together with them.
You'll report to a repeat CTO who wants thought partners: people who lay out the options, show their reasoning, and ask what we'd do if the current options disappeared. You'll also be one of a small group of technical leaders setting direction for the company. We're growing fast and working with biological systems, so designing with an experimental mindset is crucial.. You should be comfortable with ambiguity and making good calls with incomplete information.
The impact of this role is through your people. Your output is a team that ships: clear roles, managers who can build and run teams of 6-8 engineers, and cohesive system and team design. We expect you to be technically credible and fluent in how software is now built, but you won't be writing production code or doing line-by-line review.
Your Partnership With Product and Hardware
You'll join the growing director team in our technology organization, alongside our Director of Product and Director of Hardware. Together you'll deliver products with one goal: making farms as profitable and efficient as possible. We do that through the best possible breeding decisions for cattle, sensors that collect phenotypic data, and analysis built on the genomic data we collect and process.
As a team, you're accountable for keeping our existing products stable and growing their value, while prototyping, testing, and rolling out new ones.

As our Bid & Quality Manager, you’ll be the person who takes Satispay through every client tender and keeps our quality system running. This role involves managing tenders and supplier qualifications, as well as looking after our Quality Management System. You’ll work every day with Sales, Legal, Product and the heads of each department, and you’ll be the one who makes sure nothing falls through the cracks, from a tender deadline to an expiring certificate.

Here's what that looks like in practice:

- Supplier qualifications - Keep Satispay registered and up to date on our clients’ supplier portals, and work with Sales to collect and validate the documents each client asks for. Renew company documents and certifications (DURC, DURF, company registry extracts, ISO/ESG certifications) before they expire, and improve our scores with clients (IT and ESG questionnaires).

- Quality system - Keep our Quality Management System policies and procedures up to date, and guide the heads of each department so their processes are properly documented. Maintain the risk register, the list of critical suppliers and the KPI matrix linked to our quality objectives.

- KPIs and process performance - Collect data from process owners, track KPIs every quarter and go back to the owners when a KPI falls below its threshold.

- Audits and reporting - Plan the audit schedule and be the contact for external auditors. Turn quality data, audit findings and process insights into management reviews and a quarterly report on risks, suppliers and KPIs.

- Quality systems - You have experience with Quality Management Systems (such as ISO 9001 or equivalent), ideally in a service or financial services context. Audit experience is a plus.

You will work closely with venture capital partners, ecosystem organisations, and founders directly to build pipeline, convert high-value startup customers, and grow their usage of the Airwallex platform - including our AI finance and AgentOS capabilities - over time.

title: Engineering Leader
description:
The Role

As Consumer Engineering Leader, you’ll be the engineering counterpart to our Consumer Product Leader. Together you’ll own a simple question: How can we extend our product suite to be integrated deeper with our customers’ financial lives?

Engineering leadership at Taptap Send is hands on. You’ll be building POCs while managing/coaching a team of super passionate, high caliber engineers. We are looking for someone who finds themselves on the cusp of product and engineering and is excited to shape the next generation of products at a company with millions of customers. The mandate is to move fast and autonomously, understand our customers, build new products they love, and become the financial home for the immigrant communities we serve.

Key Responsibilities

- Own the Outcomes: Partner with Product to set and hit targets on adoption, retention, and how well our products serve the range of a customer’s financial life. You’re accountable for how well these products work, not just for shipping them.

- Run the Experiment Loop: Take ideas from hypothesis to live test in weeks, not quarters. Build POCs yourself. Instrument everything. Read the data honestly and recommend, kill, or scale.

- Spot the Opportunities: Bring your own ideas. You should be looking at our customers, our data, and the market and arriving with a point of view on the next unmet need worth solving.

- Ship the Winners: When a bet proves out, lead the work to harden it and get it into the core app at production quality with reliability, security, and compliance standards intact.

- Stay Hands-On: Contribute code. You set the technical direction for consumer product engineering and you’re in it with the team.

- Build and Lead a Small, High-Leverage Team: Hire, coach, and retain product-minded engineers who thrive on ambiguity and speed.

What We’re Looking For

- Product-Minded Engineers: Your background is building user-facing products and the services behind it. You’re comfortable owning a feature end-to-end, from backend through to what the user touches.

- Track Record of Rapid Experimentation: You can point to things you built in weeks that tested a real hypothesis, and to things you killed. Candidates whose experience is entirely long-horizon builds won’t be a fit.

- 0 to 1 Experience: You’ve done your best work at Series B-E companies or standing up new products/businesses within a larger company. You know what it’s like to build with real constraints and real growth pressure.

- Comfort with Compliance: You’ve shipped in regulated environments and treat compliance as a design constraint to build around from day one, not a hurdle at the end.

- Commercially Grounded: You reach for the business case before the architecture diagram. You can judge whether an idea is worth the company’s time, and you hold a high engineering bar while doing it.

- Leadership Range: You can lead and grow a team without stepping away from the technical work. This isn’t a role for someone who has moved fully into management.

Our Stack

TapTap Send is an AWS-first, polyglot engineering organisation. Across a small set of major product and platform systems, we use Kotlin/Spring Boot and Python/FastAPI for backend services, React Native/TypeScript for mobile, React/TypeScript for web, PostgreSQL for transactional data, and Redshift + dbt for analytics. You don’t need to have used all of this, but you should be able to get productive in it quickly.

Data was maintained well enough for humans to interpret. Teams know the old workarounds better than the new system. Our job is to lead that transition, from a process that is automated in parts to a process that genuinely runs on its own.

title: Associate Director/Director, Quality Assurance, CMC
description:
About Us

We are developing potentially best-in-class therapies for patients living with severe autoimmune diseases. Our lead antibody, claseprubart (DNTH103), is purposefully engineered with extended half-life, improved potency, and high selectivity for only the active C1s complement protein that drives disease pathology - enabling less frequent and more convenient self-administered subcutaneous injections. Our second clinical candidate, DNTH212 is a first and potentially best in class, bifunctional inhibitor that targets clinically validated and complementary disease modifying mechanisms, Type 1 IFN suppression and B cell modulation - enabling potential for improved clinical outcomes and patient friendly convenient, self-administered subcutaneous injections. Our newest candidate, DNTH312, is an internally developed, investigational, first-in-class, next-generation bifunctional fusion protein combining claseprubart and TACI to target potent inhibition of aC1s and BAFF/APRIL. DNTH312 aims to be Phase 1 ready by year end 2027. To learn more, please visit www.dianthustx.com  and follow us on LinkedIn .

Dianthus Therapeutics is seeking an Associate Director or Director of Quality Assurance to join our growing CMC Quality team. In this role, you will provide quality oversight across the development, manufacturing, and regulatory approval of Dianthus products, with a direct impact on the investigational medicines we deliver to patients.

Reporting to the Executive Director, Quality Assurance, you will lead QA oversight of key external manufacturing (CROs) and testing partners (CTOs) across biologics and combination products. You will partner closely with CMC Technical Operations, Manufacturing, Supply Chain, Regulatory Affairs, and Project Management, working both independently and collaboratively to resolve issues and moving multiple complex programs forward in line with corporate goals and regulatory requirements.

CMC and Manufacturing Oversight

• Ensure clinical manufacturing operations comply with cGMP requirements and Dianthus policies and procedures.

• Disposition cell banks, drug substance, and finished drug product for clinical supply, including review of executed batch records and release and stability data.

• Monitor the evolving regulatory landscape and update policies, procedures, specifications, and other quality documents accordingly.

description:
About the Team

OpenAI, in close collaboration with our capital and delivery partners, is building the infrastructure required to support frontier AI systems. The Data Center Engineering team defines repeatable technical standards and carries them through design, construction, commissioning, and operational readiness. The team works across data center facilities, power generation, compute infrastructure, construction, procurement, and operations to deliver reliable capacity at unprecedented scale and speed.

About the Role

We are seeking a Power Generation Design Engineer to help design and integrate generation plants and balance-of-plant systems for large AI data center campuses. This role spans electrical and mechanical systems, including generation equipment, campus and grid interfaces, fuel and auxiliary systems, cooling, controls, and data center loads.

The ideal candidate brings deep expertise in either electrical or mechanical engineering, along with the cross-disciplinary judgment to evaluate how the full plant operates as an integrated system. You will establish technical requirements, assess vendor and EPC solutions, resolve design interfaces, and carry systems from concept through commissioning and validated operation.

Travel: 50%

Responsibilities

- Develop and review generation-plant basis-of-design documents, design criteria, specifications, diagrams, calculations, and reference architectures.

- Define and coordinate interfaces among generation equipment, substations, campus distribution, grid connections, fuel systems, cooling, controls, and data center loads.

- Evaluate generation technologies and operating modes, including grid-connected and islanded operation, synchronization, load sharing, black start, and restoration.

- Lead or review discipline-specific engineering analyses. Electrical studies may include load flow, short circuit, arc flash, protection coordination, transient, grounding, and motor starting. Mechanical analyses may include thermal performance, hydraulics, pressure drop, ventilation, vibration, acoustics, and heat recovery.

- Review OEM and EPC proposals, equipment ratings and performance data, operating envelopes, failure modes, test plans, maintenance strategies, and lifecycle tradeoffs.

- Translate data center load profiles and operating requirements into generation-system capacity, redundancy, performance, and control requirements.

- Coordinate with electrical, mechanical, controls, CSA, fuel, utility, environmental, fire-protection, and data center engineering teams to resolve design and delivery interfaces.

- Support procurement, factory acceptance testing, construction, startup, energization, commissioning, performance testing, and root-cause investigations.

- Develop repeatable technical standards and reference designs that improve reliability, maintainability, and deployment speed across future projects.

Qualifications

- 8+ years of engineering experience in power generation, utilities, industrial systems, microgrids, oil and gas, or mission-critical infrastructure.

- Bachelor’s degree in electrical engineering, mechanical engineering, or a related field.

- Deep technical expertise in either electrical power systems or mechanical/process systems, with experience collaborating across the other discipline.

- Electrical expertise may include generators, transformers, HV/MV switchgear, protection and controls, grounding, auxiliary power, grid interconnection, and power-system studies.

- Mechanical expertise may include rotating equipment, fuel and fluid systems, piping, heat transfer, cooling, ventilation, lubrication, water treatment, exhaust, and mechanical auxiliaries.

- Experience evaluating OEM data, equipment performance, operating scenarios, failure modes, and maintenance requirements.

- Experience carrying engineering designs through construction, startup, commissioning, and operational validation.

- Ability to communicate technical risks and tradeoffs clear

description:
Rejoindre Mines Saint-Étienne , c’est s’engager dans une institution où la science et l’innovation bâtissent un avenir plus durable . Une école d’excellence où chacun a l’opportunité de révéler son plein potentiel et de contribuer à relever les défis de demain .
Classée parmi les meilleures écoles d’ingénieurs en France et reconnue mondialement, notre école, membre de l’Institut Mines-Télécom, forme les talents de demain tout en contribuant activement à relever les grands défis industriels, numériques et environnementaux. Avec nous, vous intégrez une communauté de 500 collaborateurs, 2500 étudiants, et participez à un projet ambitieux : conjuguer excellence académique, recherche d’avant-garde et impact sociétal positif.
L’Institut Mines-Télécom fédère les grandes écoles françaises autour des défis industriels majeurs, numériques, énergétiques et écologiques. Avec ses 8 Grandes Écoles publiques et 2 écoles filiales, il est le premier institut public dédié aux ingénieurs et managers. Ensemble, nous imaginons et construisons un avenir durable, en formant les acteurs qui façonneront les transitions de demain.

Bienvenue dans l’univers des matériaux du futur !
Au centre Science des Matériaux et des Structures (SMS), rattaché au Laboratoire Georges Friedel (unité mixte de recherche CNRS), on décortique la matière pour mieux la maîtriser. Alliages métalliques, céramiques, composites… ici, on explore le lien entre procédés, microstructures et propriétés des matériaux.
Grâce à des outils de caractérisation avancée et des modèles multi-échelles, nos enseignants-chercheurs inventent le concept de « Material by design » : concevoir les matériaux dès l’atelier de recherche, pour une performance sur-mesure.
🧠 Vous aimez la science fondamentale qui change le réel ? C’est ici que ça se passe.

🎯 Description du poste - ce que nous attendons de vous

Le Laboratoire Georges Friedel (LGF) est une Unité Mixte de Recherche du CNRS (UMR 5307). Situé à l’École des Mines de Saint-Étienne et porté par deux tutelles (Mines Saint-Étienne et CNRS), le laboratoire regroupe tout le potentiel de recherche de Mines Saint-Étienne dans les domaines des matériaux, de la mécanique et des procédés.
Le centre SMS - Sciences des Matériaux et des Structures - est l’un des cinq centres d’enseignement et de recherche de Mines Saint-Etienne. Au sein du LGF, il développe des recherches en science des matériaux, mécanique et procédés avancés de fabrication, pour le transport et la production d'énergie, avec un objectif d’accroître la durabilité des matériaux.

Ce post-doc s'inscrit dans le cadre de la chaire « SIRA », un partenariat de cinq ans entre Mines Saint-Etienne et les sociétés Framatome et EDF, co-financé par l'Agence Nationale de la Recherche, portant sur le vieillissement des aciers faiblement alliés (16MND5) utilisés dans les composants du circuit primaire des réacteurs nucléaires à eau pressurisée. Les travaux de la chaire incluent plusieurs doctorats et post-doctorats visant à faire progresser la connaissance du phénomène de ségrégation intergranulaire dans les aciers faiblement alliés et de la fragilisation associée, ainsi qu’à développer de nouvelles méthodologies de mesure de la ségrégation intergranulaire, ou à améliorer les méthodologies existantes.
Le post-doc proposé ici, financé par EDF, vise à déterminer l'effet de l'irradiation neutronique sur la ségrégation intergranulaire, pour les matériaux suivis dans le cadre du programme de surveillance des effets de l'irradiation sur les matériaux des cuves REP d'EDF. Il est en effet important de savoir si de la fragilisation intergranulaire peut intervenir à forte fluence pour prévoir correctement l'évolution des propriétés de rupture. C'est donc une caractérisation qui vient en appui de l'interprétation des fragilisations mesurées dans le cadre du programme de surveillance.
